episodes.189650: On the evening of April 22nd, scattered strong thunderstorms developed across southeast Nebraska at the exit of a low-level jet. A tongue of higher theta-e extended into this area from Kansas resulting in a localized area of higher instability. These thunderstorms peaked in strength just before midnight, resulting in a couple of instances of severe hail. The largest recorded hail stone was the size of a ping-pong ball.
episodes.190764: The combination of increasing low level moisture and an unstable airmass along with a weak upper level disturbance, resulted in widely scattered thunderstorms across the Big Country during the late afternoon and evening. A few of these storms became severe and produced damaging winds and isolated large hail.
episodes.190933: A quickly advancing cold front across west Texas aided in the development of isolated severe thunderstorms across the northern Permian Basin.
episodes.191122: A wet and unstable weather pattern was caused by a surface short-wave trough associated with the remnants of a frontal boundary. The Blended Total Precipitable Water (TPW) Percent of Normal indicated moisture levels exceeding 145% of the climatological normal from the Leeward Islands through the local area. A Saharan Air Layer also helped promote more frequent lightning. Flooding, Landslides (due to high soil saturation) and even a Funnel Cloud were reported under this unsettled weather. By Tuesday (23rd), USGS river sensors still indicate that most rivers over the eastern half of Puerto Rico exceeded the 75th percentile, with half of them surpassing the 90th percentile or well above normal.
episodes.191189: Severe thunderstorms resulted in several reports of large hail of around an inch in diameter on April 23rd in the vicinity of the I-96 corridor.
episodes.191228: A Plains low pressure system moving through the Upper Great Lakes produced storm force north wind gusts at Minneapolis Shoal Light during the evening of the 23rd.
